checks.claim: The executive order's goal of three test reactors critical by July 4, 2026 was met: Antares' Mark-0 (June 4, at INL), Valar Atomics' Ward 250 (June 18, Utah) and Deployable Energy's 1 MWe Unity (July 1).
checks.evidence: The July 2, 2026 ANS article gives July 1 as the day Deployable announced it had achieved zero-power criticality at INL, not a dated achievement. A July 8, 2026 Neutron Bytes article says Antares, Valar and Deployable 'completed' their demonstrations 'earlier in June'. The same Neutron Bytes article reports a fourth firm, Aalo-X, reaching criticality on 07/04/26, so the 'three' framing is also incomplete. Antares (June 4) and Valar (June 18) dates agree across both sources. Unity's achievement date is unresolved; check DOE or Deployable's own release before reusing '(July 1)' as the critical date.

checks.claim: The May 2025 orders set an 18-month ceiling on NRC decisions for new reactors and created the DOE Reactor Pilot Program, which authorizes test reactors at DOE sites under DOE's own safety authority rather than NRC licensing.
checks.evidence: The May 2025 nuclear executive order ('Ordering the Reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission') sets a deadline of no more than 18 months for final NRC decision on an application to construct and operate a new reactor of any type (Section 5(a)(1)). The same order requires NRC to issue final rules within 18 months, which puts the final-rule deadline at 2026-11-23. Only the 18-month clause was verified here; the DOE Reactor Pilot Program clause was not checked against this page.
